ns2:section.sectionText: TOPIC: Soviet Literature After 1956. This course covers material from the second half of the 20th century, with emphasis on Soviet literature and culture after Stalin. Stalin?s death in 1953 marked a turning point for the Soviet Union: the revolutionary enthusiasm of the twenties was replaced by the terror of the thirties and the trauma of the Second World War. High Stalinism had brought with it a belief in the power of the State and the cult of its Leader, as well as a return to middle-class values as the possibility of prosperity seemed just around the corner and the bright future lay just ahead. The forties witnessed the near destruction of the country during the war and the aftermath of the purges, arrests, executions, and wartime devastation. At the same time, however, the Soviet Union emerged from the war a true Super-power, with atomic capabilities and a stranglehold on almost half of Europe (as well as a major influence in Asia, Africa, South America, and Cuba). This course starts with Nikita Khrushchev?s ?Secret Speech? at the 20th Party Congress in 1956 that began the process of de-Stalinization. The class will focus on the period 1956-2000, looking at the second half of the Soviet twentieth century. Throughout the course we will screen a number of films along with novels, short stories, and theoretical texts, which will provide a common base for thinking about late and post-Soviet culture.
